Asha —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we finalize the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and lock in the evaluation window, procurement asked for a short, reviewable cost sanity for the MAP so they can include it in the PO/term sheet. I attached a v2 MAP and a token-econ spreadsheet with our working numbers.

Two asks from our side to make the evaluation run smoothly:
- Confirm target evaluation SLOs (latency percentiles) and any hard caps on monthly spend.
- Confirm whether the dataset includes long-prefixed dialogs (i.e., repeated system prompts) so we can model caching benefits accurately.

High-level assumptions we used in the attached spreadsheet (we can update):
- Typical round-trip = prompt (avg 420 tokens) + response (avg 380 tokens) => ~800 tokens per call
- Default batching window: 100ms, optimistic average effective batch size = 6-8 for peak workloads
- Prefix/KV caching expected to reduce prompt tokens by ~25-35% for repeated flows
- Two pricing scenarios modeled: 
  * Hosted standard model: $0.00008 / token (=> ~12,500 tokens / $1)
  * Dedicated discounted: $0.00006 / token (=> ~16,667 tokens / $1)

If you can confirm the evaluation dataset characteristics and any internal target for tokens/$ we will produce a short one-page appendix to add to the MAP that procurement can include with the PO.

Regards,

Ben Carter

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the details on traffic split. I ran a quick appendix with conservative and optimistic caching scenarios and a three-tiered calls table (10k / 100k / 1M). Highlights below and I attached the quick-run CSV with line-item math.

Assumptions (explicit):
1) Round-trip tokens per call (no caching): prompt 420 + response 380 = 800 tokens
2) Caching: conservative = 10% prompt token reduction, optimistic = 35% prompt token reduction
3) Batching: we model a 100ms batching window with effective batch size 6 for steady traffic, up to 8 at peaks. Batching reduces per-call host overhead but does not reduce token counts; it lowers per-token inference overhead and therefore effective per-token price in Dedicated scenarios via utilization improvements (we quantify as a 15% economic improvement at batch size 6).
4) Pricing used in table: Hosted = $0.00008 / token; Dedicated = $0.00006 / token. Dedicated line shows discounted rate after commit.

Sample math (conservative scenario, 100k calls/month with 60% intake / 40% summarization):
- Intake calls (60k): intake prompt average 540 tokens (long system prompt) + response 300 tokens = 840 tokens. With conservative caching (10% prompt reuse) -> average prompt tokens drop from 540 to 486 => average intake tokens = 786.
- Summarization calls (40k): prompt 200 + response 600 = 800 tokens (no caching expected).
- Weighted avg tokens/call = ((60k*786) + (40k*800)) / 100k = 791 tokens/call.
- Total tokens for 100k calls = 79,100,000 tokens.
- Cost (Hosted): 79,100,000 * $0.00008 = $6,328.
- Cost (Dedicated w/ batching econ improvement 15%): effective token cost = $0.00006 * 0.85 = $0.000051 => 79,100,000 * $0.000051 = $4,034.1

Buckets (Hosted, conservative caching):
- 10k calls -> ~7,910,000 tokens -> $632.8
- 100k calls -> ~79,100,000 tokens -> $6,328
- 1M calls -> ~791,000,000 tokens -> $63,280

Optimistic caching reduces intake prompt tokens to 351 (35% off 540), which drops weighted avg tokens/call to ~757 and lowers all bucket costs by ~4.3-5%. I'll include both columns in the CSV.

Links attached: technical_runbook.md (how we count tokens & recommended batching configs), nimblehealth_token_econ_spreadsheet.csv (line-by-line math).

SOC 2: https://redwoodinference.com/compliance/SOC2-report (public attestation; we can provide redacted report on request).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to share the one-page appendix (procurement-facing) with the three bucket examples + conservative/optimistic rows.
- Schedule MAP sign-off call next Tue/Thu — proposing Tue 2/16 10am PT.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
